To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) We have developed a numerical method for solving lattice-refined models of loop quantum cosmological systems, and (2) We have found that, for a lattice-refined model of loop quantum cosmologies, the wave function is stable under a uniform lattice refinement, but unstable under a non-uniform lattice refinement.

we have developed a method that can be used to solve the constraint equations in any lattice-refining model, and we have investigated the ''motion'' due to the underlying discretization in both constant and variable lattice models.

we have proposed a numerical method for solving lattice-refined difference equations in the context of loop quantum cosmological models, and that we have confirmed the stability criterion of the difference equations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis and solution of the quantum constraint equation for generic lattice refinement models in loop quantum gravity.
the numerical treatment of the quantum constraint equation for generic lattice-refined cosmological models, and with the study of the effects of the underlying discreteness on the wave function.
the development and application of numerical methods for the solution of lattice refinement models in loop quantum gravity.

the numerical technique we developed can be applied in a wide variety of lattice-refined models.
